title: STDD project configuration
description: Schema for .stdd.config.yml. Declares project structure, commands, docs layout, workflow options, and plugins consumed by stdd skills and agents.

version.description: Config format version. Currently 1. Used for future migration of the config layout. Optional.

name.description: Short identifier for the project. Kebab-case recommended (e.g. 'my-app').

language.description: Preferred natural-language for skill / agent output. Currently only 'ja' and 'en' are supported by core skills; additional locales require new translations to be contributed.

apps.description: List of applications inside the repository. At least one app is required.

id.description: Short identifier used in docs paths and command substitution. Lowercase, may contain digits, underscore, or hyphen. Examples: 'web', 'admin', 'user_app'.

path.description: Filesystem path (relative to repo root) where this app's source lives. Examples: 'apps/web', 'user_app'.

port.description: Optional dev-server port for this app. Used by E2E config and worktree port allocation.

framework.description: Optional informational tag (e.g. 'nextjs', 'remix', 'sveltekit'). Plugins may key off this value.

commands.description: Commands stdd will execute on behalf of the project. Define them so skills do not need to hardcode tooling.

typecheck.description: Command that performs static type checking and exits 0 on success. Example: 'npx tsc --noEmit'.

test.description: Default test runner command. Example: 'npm test', 'pnpm test', 'vitest run'.

build.description: Production build command. Used by the pre-push hook and QA flow. Example: 'npm run build'. Optional.

dev.description: Command that starts the local dev server (long-running). Used by the QA flow for browser smoke verification via Playwright MCP, combined with apps[].port to build the URL. Example: 'npm run dev'. Optional — when omitted, the browser verification step is skipped.

db_reset.description: Command to reset the local database to a known seeded state. Optional.

db_types.description: Command to regenerate database-derived TypeScript / language types. Optional.

docs.description: Documentation layout used by spec / plan skills.

lineup.description: Line-up of the feature-tier technical specs. 'single' (default; existing installs): one TECH_DESIGN.md and one TEST_PLAN.md per feature. 'layered' (default for new installs): backend and frontend are designed separately — API_DESIGN.md + API_TEST_DESIGN.md, SCREEN_DESIGN.md + SCREEN_TEST_DESIGN.md, and the feature-wide TEST_DESIGN.md. A backend-only or frontend-only feature set may omit one side. See packages/core/docs/spec-lineup.md.

structure.description: Overrides of section names, table column names, table row labels, and row-ID prefixes of spec documents. Defaults per language are in skills/documenting-tech-specs/references/doc-structure.json; checkers read the override first. Keys are the language-independent identifiers used in that file. Example: { api_design: { sections: { operations: 'エンドポイント' }, tables: { response_codes: { columns: { condition: '条件' } } } } }.

sections.description: Section key -> section name (without the number).

layout.description: Path templates that map an app + feature to its documentation files. Handlebars variables available: {{app.id}}, {{app.path}}, {{feature_path}}, {{date}}. {{app.*}} resolves against each entry of the top-level `apps[]`. Note: test file layout (e2e / integration / unit paths) is intentionally out of scope for this schema in Phase 1-A; templates currently assume conventional layouts and Phase 1-B may introduce a separate `tests.layout` object.

common_requirements.description: Optional path template for the project-wide (common tier) REQUIREMENTS.md — the whole-service business requirements overview. No app/feature variables apply. Example: 'docs/common/REQUIREMENTS.md'. Omit when the project does not use a common tier.

common_architecture.description: Optional path template for the project-wide (common tier) ARCHITECTURE.md — the whole-service system overview (構成・スタック・連携・セキュリティ・インフラ). Data model and API are split into common_table_definition / common_api_spec. Part of the technical specs (tech_specs). No app/feature variables apply. Example: 'docs/common/ARCHITECTURE.md'. Omit when the project does not use a common tier.

common_table_definition.description: Optional path template for the project-wide (common tier) TABLE_DEFINITION.md — the single source of truth for all table/column definitions. Feature TECH_DESIGN.md references it instead of redefining schema. Part of the technical specs (tech_specs). No app/feature variables apply. Example: 'docs/common/TABLE_DEFINITION.md'. Omit when the project does not use a common tier.

common_api_spec.description: Optional path template for the project-wide (common tier) API_SPEC.md — the single source of truth for API contracts (OpenAPI-style Markdown). Feature TECH_DESIGN.md references it. Part of the technical specs (tech_specs). No app/feature variables apply. Example: 'docs/common/API_SPEC.md'. Omit for projects without a custom API (e.g. direct DB access).

common_design.description: Optional path template for the project-wide (common tier) DESIGN.md — design standards (tokens / component conventions / layout). Part of the technical specs (tech_specs). No app/feature variables apply. Example: 'docs/common/DESIGN.md'. Omit when the project does not maintain design standards.

tech_design.description: Path template for TECH_DESIGN.md (概要 / 設計判断 / 画面項目定義 / 処理ロジック / エラーハンドリング / 非機能要件). Part of the technical specs (tech_specs). Same variables as 'requirements'. Required when docs.lineup is 'single' (or omitted).

test_plan.description: Path template for TEST_PLAN.md — the feature's test strategy (use-case to test-level mapping). Split out of TECH_DESIGN. Part of the technical specs (tech_specs). Same variables as 'requirements'. Example: 'docs/{{app.id}}/{{feature_path}}/TEST_PLAN.md'. Required when docs.lineup is 'single' (or omitted).

api_design.description: Path template for API_DESIGN.md (docs.lineup 'layered') — the semantics of the feature's API operations: per-operation info table, response codes and when each is returned, procedure, response specification, state transitions, feature rules, other process flows. Same variables as 'requirements'. Example: 'docs/{{app.id}}/{{feature_path}}/API_DESIGN.md'. Requires api_test_design.

screen_design.description: Path template for SCREEN_DESIGN.md (docs.lineup 'layered') — screen items with IDs, validation / event / response-handling tables, and the text and state catalog. Same variables as 'requirements'. Example: 'docs/{{app.id}}/{{feature_path}}/SCREEN_DESIGN.md'. Requires screen_test_design.

api_test_design.description: Path template for API_TEST_DESIGN.md (docs.lineup 'layered') — one row per API_DESIGN row (operation x code, transition, rule, flow) with test level and test reference. Same variables as 'requirements'.

screen_test_design.description: Path template for SCREEN_TEST_DESIGN.md (docs.lineup 'layered') — one row per SCREEN_DESIGN row (items with conditions, validations, events, response handling). Same variables as 'requirements'.

test_design.description: Path template for TEST_DESIGN.md (docs.lineup 'layered') — the feature-wide test design: coverage of every use case and acceptance criterion, E2E scenarios, cross-feature rules, and what is not tested. Same variables as 'requirements'. Required when docs.lineup is 'layered'.

wireframes.description: Optional path template for the HTML wireframes directory generated by the generating-wireframes skill. Same variables as 'requirements'. Example: 'docs/{{app.id}}/{{feature_path}}/wireframes/'. When omitted, skills default to a 'wireframes/' directory next to REQUIREMENTS.md.

plan.description: Optional path template for PLAN documents. Additional variable: {{date}} (yyyy-mm-dd of the session). Omit when the project does not keep PLAN documents; skills then skip PLAN creation (auto-implement Phase 1.5) and implement directly from TEST_PLAN.md.

workflow.description: Optional workflow toggles. Skills consult these to enable / disable worktree- and devcontainer-aware code paths.

branch_prefix.description: Prefix applied to branches created by stdd skills (e.g. 'claude/'). Skills read this instead of hardcoding a prefix. Optional; defaults to 'claude/'.

enforce_spec_first.description: Behavior of the spec-first PreToolUse hook (.claude/hooks/spec-first-check.sh) that nudges the Spec -> Test -> Implementation order on ad-hoc edits. 'off': disabled. 'warn' (default): inject a non-blocking reminder when editing an implementation file. 'block': deny implementation edits when the current branch has no Spec / test change yet. Spec, test, docs, .claude, and config / lockfile edits are always exempt.

enforce_agent_scope.description: Behavior of the agent-scope PreToolUse hook (.claude/hooks/agent-scope-guard.sh). Applies only to subagent calls of the reviewers (requirements-reviewer / tech-specs-reviewer / test-reviewer / code-reviewer). Reviewers may not write files and may run only one read-only shell command per call. 'off': disabled. 'warn' (default): report the violation in context without stopping. 'block': deny the operation.

enforce_worktree_lock.description: Behavior of the worktree-lock PreToolUse hook (.claude/hooks/worktree-lock-guard.sh). When the session has declared its working tree with skills/auto-implement/scripts/worktree-lock.sh lock, subagent edits and shell working directories outside the declared tree are reported. Sessions without a declaration are not affected. 'off': disabled. 'warn' (default): report without stopping. 'block': deny the operation.

enforce_test_scope.description: Behavior of the test-scope PreToolUse hook (.claude/hooks/test-scope-guard.sh). Reports running commands.test without any target argument (a full run) outside the QA phase. qa-engineer subagents and commands prefixed with STDD_FULL_TEST_REASON="<reason>" are exempt. 'off': disabled. 'warn' (default): report without stopping. 'block': deny the command.

enabled.description: Whether the project uses git worktrees for parallel development.

script.description: Path to the project's worktree creation script. Required when 'enabled' is true.

port_base.description: Base port number used to derive per-worktree port offsets.

override_config.description: Path to a devcontainer override config used by the worktree flow.

response_codes.description: Overrides for the response-code system (skills/documenting-tech-specs/guides/response-codes.md). The bands (0 normal / 1 user-recoverable rejection / 9 not recoverable by the user) and the granularity (one code per terminating branch) are fixed by STDD; the feature-code format and the list of common codes can be overridden here. Optional; omitted keys use the guide's defaults.

feature_code_pattern.description: Regular expression for the feature code that prefixes every response code (e.g. 'ORD' in 'ORD-1001').

common_codes.description: List of common codes. When present it replaces the default list in the guide (VALIDATION_ERROR 1800, AUTH_REQUIRED 9800, NOT_FOUND 9820, INTERNAL_ERROR 9900).

default_behavior.description: Default screen behavior when a screen receives this code.

traceability.description: ID-based traceability configuration. Assigns stable IDs to requirements (use cases / flows) and threads them through tech design, tests, and implementation so that the requirement -> design -> test -> implementation chain and its gaps can be detected mechanically (by the verifying-consistency skill and the trace-audit.sh scanner). Optional; when omitted, traceability auditing is skipped.

enabled.description: Whether ID-based traceability auditing is active. When false, the audit and enforcement are skipped.

enforce.description: Enforcement level for traceability gaps, mirroring workflow.enforce_spec_first. 'off': never fail. 'warn' (default): report gaps without failing. 'block': the pre-push hook (and CI) fail when gaps are found. Recommended to start at 'warn' and raise to 'block' once the project is mature.

id_prefixes.description: ID prefixes for each traceable unit. Defaults: use_case=UC, flow=FL, acceptance=AC.

use_case.description: Prefix for use-case IDs (REQUIREMENTS §2.1). Example produces 'UC-<feature>-NN'.

flow.description: Prefix for other-process-flow IDs (TECH_DESIGN §4.2). Example produces 'FL-<feature>-NN'.

acceptance.description: Prefix for optional acceptance-criterion IDs. Example produces 'AC-<feature>-NN-k'. Only used when tracing at acceptance-criterion granularity.

patterns.description: Regular expressions describing how tests and implementation reference IDs. Adjust to match the project's test framework and annotation convention. Capture group 1 must isolate the ID.

test_tag.description: Regex matching an ID reference inside a test title. Default convention wraps the ID in brackets. Example: '\\[((UC|FL)-[a-z0-9]+-[0-9]+)\\]'.

impl_annotation.description: Regex matching an ID annotation inside implementation source. Default convention uses an '@stdd <ID>' marker comment. Example: '@stdd\\s+((UC|FL)-[a-z0-9]+-[0-9]+)'.

scan.description: Glob patterns (relative to repo root) that the scanner walks to collect test tags and implementation annotations.

require_impl_annotation.description: When true, a use case with no '@stdd' implementation annotation is reported as a gap (blocking under enforce='block') rather than a warning. When false (default), missing implementation annotations are warnings only, since implementation coverage is otherwise established transitively through tagged tests.

feedback.description: Development-feedback loop: process issues found during a work unit are filed as GitHub issues before the PR is created (recording-dev-feedback skill) and periodically aggregated (measuring-dev-process skill). Read by the bundled script skills/recording-dev-feedback/scripts/dev-feedback.sh. Optional; every key has a default. See packages/core/docs/feedback-loop.md.

enabled.description: Whether the feedback triage step runs before PR creation. When false, the skills skip filing and the scripts exit without doing anything.

labels.description: GitHub label names. Change them to match the project's language or naming; the scripts and skills read them from here.

base.description: Label that distinguishes feedback issues from ordinary work issues. Open issues with this label mean 'not yet reflected'.

priority_high.description: Priority label: reflect before starting the next work unit.

priority_medium.description: Priority label: reflect before more features are added. Subject to the stale rule (stale_days).

category_prefix.description: Prefix for category labels. The category keys themselves (spec-format, skill, agent, automation, flow, coding-rules, other) are fixed by the feedback rules.

max_issues_per_pr.description: Upper bound of feedback issues filed from one work unit (one PR). Recurrence comments on existing issues are not counted.

stale_days.description: A medium-priority open issue with no activity for this many days becomes a candidate for closing as 'not planned'. Applied by a person at measurement time, never on a schedule.

recurrence_to_high.description: Number of recurrence comments (lines starting with '再発 —') from repository members at which a medium-priority issue is raised to high.

registry.description: Path of the improvement registry (measurement history, measures and their verdicts, rulings, rejected ideas, known instrument issues). Created from the measuring-dev-process template on first use.

telemetry.description: Per-PR process telemetry posted as a PR comment right after PR creation (create-pr skill, script skills/create-pr/scripts/pr-telemetry.sh). Holds only review-process-independent fields: size, durations, review rounds / exemption, and feedback triage counts. Optional.

enabled.description: Whether create-pr posts the telemetry comment. When false, step recording and posting are skipped.

emergency_mode.description: Emergency work mode (choosing-work-mode skill). Only the user can enter it: the UserPromptSubmit hook hooks/work-mode-prompt.sh records the user's explicit mention, and skills/choosing-work-mode/scripts/work-mode.sh refuses to declare without that record. On an emergency branch, delegation to specialist agents, review rounds, and passing quality gates are not required (Spec -> Test -> Implementation order is kept), and the PR body must state that it was made in emergency mode. Optional; every key has a default. See packages/core/docs/work-modes-and-limits.md.

enabled.description: Whether emergency mode can be used in this project. When false, the hook records nothing, declaration is refused, and every branch stays in normal mode.

request_ttl_minutes.description: How long (minutes) the user's recorded mention of emergency mode stays valid for one declaration.

models.description: Model selection for Claude Code only (packages/core/docs/model-selection.md). Values are model aliases, never model IDs. Codex outputs are not affected. Optional.

agents.description: Per-agent model override, keyed by agent name (e.g. qa-engineer). Applied to the 'model' line of .claude/agents/<name>.md when 'stdd init' runs. Agents not listed keep the shipped default (see model-selection.md §2).

mechanical.description: Model passed to subagents that skills delegate mechanical work to (wide search, summarizing logs). 'inherit' means pass no model (use the main conversation's model).

plugins.description: Plugins loaded in addition to core skills/agents. Each entry may be a short string id or an object with options.

oneOf.description: Short plugin id. Resolves to npm package '@stdd/plugin-<id>' by convention.

id.description: Plugin id (same resolution rules as the string form).

options.description: Plugin-specific options. Validated by the plugin's own schema, not by this schema.

modelAlias.description: Claude Code model alias. 'inherit' uses the main conversation's model. Model IDs are not allowed because they go stale when new models ship.
